Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
(Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
)
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Tamil Nadu 58
of 1961). - Having regard to the recommendations of the Planning Commission in the Second Five-Year Plan for
reducing the glaring inequalities in the ownership of agricultural land, the Government have decided to undertake
legislation for prescribing the maximum extent of agricultural land that a person may hold. The ceiling will, except as
otherwise provided in the Bill, apply to all agricultural lands held by a person either as owner or as an usufructuary
mortgagee or as a tenant or as an intermediary or in one or more of those capacities. The provisions of the Bill will apply
to the whole of the State of Madras. The Bill contains provisions for controlling future acquisition of agricultural land.

2. The provisions of the Bill are explained in Notes on Clauses.
Published in Part IV-A of the Fort St. George Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 16th April 1960.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1967
(Tamil Nadu Act 22 of l967). - Section 59 of the Madras Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Madras
Act
58 of 1961
) originally provided that the provisions of Chapter VIII of that Act shall remain in force for a period of three years from
the date of publication of the Act, namely, the 2nd May 1962. The life of this chapter was extended by three years by the
Madras Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1965 (Madras Act 10 of 1965). The chapter will
now expire on the 2nd May 1968.

2. Chapter VIII of the Act deals with the cultivating tenant's ceiling area. The proposal to enact a single Comprehensive
Tenancy Act embodying all the tenancy enactments in force in the State including Chapter VIII of the Madras Land
Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, with suitable modifications with reference to the recommendations
made by the Planning Commission, the Government of India etc., from time to time is separately under the
Consideration of the Government. This Comprehensive Tenancy Bill is hot likely to come up before the expiry of the life
of Chapter VIII of the Madras Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961. It has, therefore, been decided to
amend section 59 of the Madras Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Madras Act
58 of 1961
) so as to extend the life of Chapter VIII for a further period of two years form the 2nd May 1968.

3. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 3,of the Fort St. George Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 25th November 1967.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1970
(Tamil Nadu Act 9 of 1970). - Section 59 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Tamil
Nadu Act
58 of 1961
) originally provided that the provisions of Chapter VIII of that Act, relating to cultivating tenant's ceiling area, shall
remain in force for a period of three years from the date of publication of the Act, namely, the 2nd May 1962. By the
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1965 (Tamil Nadu Act 10 of 1965), the life of
this chapter was extended by three years from the 2nd May 1965. The life of this chapter was further extended by
another two years by the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1967 (Tamil Nadu
Act 22 of 1967). The chapter will now expire on the 2nd May 1970.

2. A proposal to enact a single comprehensive Tenancy Act is separately under consideration of the Government. This
proposal is not likely to materialise before the expiry of the life of the said Chapter VIII. The Government have therefore
decided to amend section 59 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
) so as to extend the life of Chapter VIII for a further period of two years from the 2nd May 1970.

3. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 3 page 62 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 4th April 1970.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1970 (Tamil Nadu
Act 17 of 1970). - According to section 5 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, the
ceiling area in the case of every person and in the case of every family consisting of not more than five members, is 30
standard acres. Even after the implementation of the said Act, there is disparity in the ownership of agricultural land
leading to the concentration of such land in the hands of certain persons to the common detriment. As a further step
towards 'agrarian reform it is considered necessary to reduce such disparity. With a view to achieve this object it is
considered necessary to reduce the ceiling area from 30 standard acres to 15 standard acres.
The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 3 page 54 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 31st March

1970.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1970 (Tamil Nadu
Act 17 of 1970). - According to section 5 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, the
ceiling area in the case of every person and in the case of every family consisting of not more than five members, is 30

Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
standard acres. Even after the implementation of the said Act, there is disparity in the ownership of agricultural land
leading to the concentration of such land in the hands of certain persons to the common detriment. As a further step
towards agrarian reform, it is considered necessary to reduce such disparity. With a view to achieve this object, it is
considered necessary to reduce the ceiling area from 30 standard acres to 15 standard acres.
The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 31st March 1970.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1971
(Tamil Nadu Act 41 of 1971). - Under the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, the ceiling
area in the case of every person and in the case of every family consisting of not more than five members, was 30
standard acres. Even after the implementation of the said Act, there has been disparity in the ownership of agricultural
land leading to the concentration of such land in the hands of certain persons to the common detriment. Therefore, by
the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1970, the Government reduced the ceiling area from
30 standard acres to 15 standard acres.

2. As a further step towards agrarian reform and for the effective implementation of the Act, the Government decided to
review the exemptions contained in the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961. Accordingly,
a Committee consisting of legislators of both the Houses was constituted to go into the question and recommend on the
continuance or otherwise of the various exemptions contained in the Land Ceiling Act of 1961. The Committee has also
recommended that the exemptions contained in the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 in
respect of lands used exclusively for grazing and assessed to land revenue at Rs. 1.25 and below per acre and lands
used for the cultivation of sugar-cane and in respect of which the Sugar Factory Board has granted permission under
section 40 or 43 of the Act, may be deleted. The Government have accepted the recommendation of the Committee and
have decided to withdraw the exemption in regard to the two items mentioned above.

3. Provision has been made in the Bill for acquisition of surplus land held by Sugar Factories and for cultivation of such
land by a corporation (including a company) owned or controlled by the State. The lands held on a tenancy basis which
is within the ceiling area of the landowner shall be deemed to be held on a tenancy basis by the corporation to ensure
continued supply of sugar-cane to the factory. Such land will be held by the factory only till the expiry of the period of
contract of tenancy. An extent of land not exceeding 100 standard acres held by the sugar factory solely for research
and seed farm purposes has also been exempted from the operation of the Act.

4. Provision has been made to the effect that the surplus land acquired from the sugar factory may be redistributed in
accordance with the rules made under section 94. Incidental provision for the abolition of the Sugar Factory Board and
the Sugar Factory Tribunal has also been made.

5. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 7th July 1971.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1972
(Tamil Nadu Act 20 of 1972). - Section 59 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
(Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
), originally provided that the provisions of Chapter VIII of that Act relating to cultivating tenant's ceiling area shall remain
in force for a period of three years from the date of the publication of the Act, namely, the 2nd May 1962. The life of this
Chapter was extended, from time to time, by legislation. By the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land)
Amendment Act, 1970 (Tamil Nadu Act 9 of 1970), the life of this Chapter was last extended up to the 1st May 1972.
The life of this Chapter will expire on the 2nd May 1972. The Government have decided to retain this Chapter
permanently by omitting section 59 of the Act.

2. The Bill seeks to achieve the above object.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 28th March 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Second Amendment Act,
1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 20 of 1972). - Under sub-section (5) of section 5 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of
Ceiling on Land Act, 1961 (Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
), the maximum extent of land which a family consisting of more than five members can hold is 60 standard acres. It has
been decided to reduce this maximum extent from 60 standard acres to 40 standard acres.
Page 3/83
 
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961

2. The Committee of Legislators of both Houses constituted to review the exemptions contained in the Tamil Nadu Land
Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961, has recommended the deletion of the exemption in respect of hill areas
contained in section 73(v) of the Act. The Government have accepted this recommendation and the Bill seeks to give
effect to the deletion of the exemption in respect of hill areas.

3. Sub-clause (2) of clause (40) of section 3 of Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
prescribes the formula for conversion of ordinary acres into standard acres in respect of lands in the Kanyakumari
district. The wet lands irrigated by rain-fed tanks in Kanyakumari district are not covered by this formula. It has,
therefore, been decided to amend sub-clause (2) of clause (40) of section 3 so as to treat the wet-lands irrigated by
rain-fed tanks in the Kanyakumari district to be on a par with the dry lands irrigated by rain-fed tanks for the purpose of
calculation of standard acre.

4. Under section 60 of the said Act, the cultivating tenant's ceiling area means 5 standard acres. According to sub-rule
(2-A) of rule 51 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Rules, 1962, where the authorized officer
finds that the land held by a cultivating tenant excess of the cultivating tenant's ceiling area is more than 1/2 an acre in
the case of wet lands and one acre in the case of dry lands, the authorized officer may for reasons to be recorded in
writing leave such excess land in the possession of the cultivating tenant. On the recommendation of the Committee on
Subordinate Legislation, it has been decided to incorporate the above provision in the Act by amending section 62
suitably, as it was felt that the power given under the rules to the authorized officer to allow any land in excess of the
cultivating tenant's ceiling area to remain with the tenant would not be proper.

5. According to clause (iv) of section 73 of the said Act, nothing contained in the Act will apply to any land held by any
industrial or commercial undertaking other than a co-operative society which in the opinion of the Government bona fide
carries on industrial or commercial operation and which is approved by the Government. Under this section, if the
approval is given by the Government, then, the industrial or commercial undertaking can hold any extent of land. There
is no power under this section to restrict the extent of land in respect of which the undertaking should enjoy the
exemptions. It has, therefore, now been decided to provide in new section 37-A that an industrial or commercial
undertaking should apply to the Government for permission to hold or acquire land in excess of the ceiling area. The
exemption will be applicable only in respect of those lands specified in the order granting permission, provided that the
conditions specified in the order granting exemption are complied with.

6. Section 111 of the said Act empowers the Government to issue orders to remove any difficulty that may arise in giving
effect to any of the provisions of the Act. The Supreme Court in Messrs. Jalan Trading Company v. Mill Mazdoor Sabha
[1967] 1 SCJ 189 has observed that the power to remove difficulty by altering the provisions of the Act would in
substance amount to exercise of legislative authority and that such power cannot be delegated to an executive authority.
This opportunity has, therefore, been availed of to omit section 111.

7. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects. This Bill attempts to make the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of
Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 a comprehensive one by incorporating provisions which are in line with the change of time
and which are really beneficial to the tillers of the soil. It may be remembered that before the Act came into force, there
were large scale transactions resulting in benami alienations of lands in order to defeat the very purpose of this Act and
in fact the surplus land declared was negligible in contrast to the vast tract of land in our State. Several agitations were
carried on and many people laid their lives to rectify such loop-holes. Further, even the ceiling fixed in the Act, was not in
tune with the public demand. Taking the demands from the public and of the progressive movements, amendments
have been proposed in this Bill. If the proposed amendments are carried out, it means:-
Absentee landlordism is abolished for ever; tenant is given his option to purchase the land comprised in his holding at a
very reasonable price; tenant is granted fixity of tenure and the safeguard not to be evicted under no circumstances;
small landholders is protected from his land; ceiling limit to which a person or family is entitled to hold is reduced;
exemption granted under the present Act is totally removed except in the case of the Government lands; and ways and
means are provided for disposal of the land to the landless poor.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 30th March 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Third Amendment Act,
1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 37 of 1972). - Under section 73F(ii) of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land)
Act, 1961, the ceiling limit will not apply to any land held by-
(a) any charitable or educational institution of a public nature;
Page 4/83
 
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
(b) any trust;
(c) any University constituted by any law.
According to section 3(49) "Trust" means Trust for a public purpose of a religious or charitable or of an educational
nature and any temple, math, mosque, church or other place, by includes whatever name known which is dedicated to,
or for the benefit of, or used as of right by any community or section thereof as a place of public religious worship.
Section 2 of the Act says that nothing contained in the Act shall apply to lands held by religious Trusts of a public nature.

2. In the budget speech presented on 1st March 1972, the Chief Minister announced that all exemptions in favour of
trusts created after 26th January 1950 the date on which our Constitution came into force would be withdrawn except for
a limited extent to be allowed for trusts for educational purposes and medical facilities.

3. The Government have examined the matter further. They have decided that lands held by religious institutions as
patta lands should continue to be exempted from the Land Ceiling Act. They have also decided that "Trust" as such
need not continue to be exempted whether such Trust is created before or after the 26th January 1950. However, the
Government have examined the requirements of various Colleges, High Schools and Hospitals in the State. After taking
all relevant aspects into consideration, they have decided that in the case of colleges which are mentioned in Part I of
Schedule I, the ceiling area will be 60 standard acres. In the case of High Schools which are mentioned in Part II of
Schedule I, the ceiling area will be 20 standard acres. In the case of hospitals mentioned in Part III of Schedule I, the
ceiling area will be the extent of the land held by such hospital as on the 1st March 1972. These hospitals cannot
acquire in future any land in excess of the land already held by them on 1st March 1972.

4. The ceiling area in pursuance of the Bill, when enacted into law, will be fixed with reference to the 1st day of March
1972, the date on which the Chief Minister made the announcement in the budget speech.

5. The Bill seeks to achieve the above objects.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 3rd April 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Fourth Amendment Act,
1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 39 of 1972). - The Committee of legislators of both the Houses constituted to review the
exemptions contained in the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act 1961 has recommended the
deletion of the exemption in respect of lands used for dairy farming or live-stock breeding contained in section 73(x) of
the Act. The Government have accepted the recommendation of the Committee.

2. Consequent on the deletion of the exemption in respect of lands used for dairy farming or live-stock breeding, the
functions of the Land Board will be confined only to grant of permission under section 31 of the Act to hold lands
interspersed among or contiguous to any plantation. The Government have, therefore, decided to change the
constitution of the Land Board.

3. Under sub-section (5) of section 5 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961 (Tamil
Nadu Act
58 of 1961
), as amended by the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Second Amendment Act (Tamil Nadu Act
20 of 1972), the maximum extent of land which a family consisting more than five members can hold is 40 standard
acres. It has been decided to reduce this maximum extent from 40 standard acres to 30 standard acres, viz., twice the
extent allowed for a family consisting of five members or less.

4. The High Court has held that a person who has a right to enjoy the land during his life time without a power to alienate
is not a limited owner as defined in clause (28) of section 3 of the Act. It has, therefore, been decided to amend this
section to the effect that a person who has right to enjoy the land during his life time shall be deemed to be a limited
owner notwithstanding that he has no power to alienate the land. This amendment take effect from 6th April 1960 which
is the date of commencement of Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
.

5. At present there is no power vested in any authority to reopen a case finalised under the Act, if for any reason the
extent of any land held by a person has been omitted to be included in the total extent of the land held by such person
for the purposes of the Act. It has, therefore, been decided to insert a new provision giving power to the Land
Commissioner to direct authorised officer to reopen the cases in cases of omission of land to be included in the total
extent held by a person.

6. Section 8(1) allows a time limit of 90 days for filing returns by a person holding land in excess of the ceiling limit.
Page 5/83
 
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
Section 10(5) allows 60 days time to file objections by a person interested in the land in respect of which draft statement
has been published. Section 50(2) allows 60 plus 30 days time for preferring claim for compensation for the land
acquired. Section 50(3)(a)(ii) allows 60 plus 30 days time for preferring objections to the draft compensation assessment
roll. Section 51(1) allows 90 days time for preferring claims by mortgagees or charge holders of the land acquired.
Section 78(1) allows 60 days time to land holders to file appeal to the Land Tribunal against the decision of the
authorised officer. The time now allowed for filing returns, filing of objections, etc., under the various provisions referred
to above is considered too long as this leads to prolongation of the proceedings of the Act in each case resulting in delay
in the implementation of the Act. It has, therefore, been decided to reduce the time allowed under the various sections
referred to above except section 51(1) to 30 days and to reduce the time allowed under section 51(1) to 60 days.

7. It has been decided to omit the existing section 81 of the Act relating to the revisional jurisdiction of the Land Tribunal
and to entrust the revisional jurisdiction to the Land Commissioner in respect of the matters specified in that section.

8. At the conference of Chief Ministers held on 23rd July 1972 at New Delhi, it was decided that the compensation for
surplus land acquired should be on a slab basis with the quantum decreasing with increase in the size of the holding.
The existing provision in Schedule HI to Act
58 of 1961
provides for calculation of the compensation on the basis of the multiples of net annual income. The net annual income
is the amount of fair rent less the land revenue. It has been decided to revise the slabs prescribed in paragraph 6 of Part
I of Schedule III for purposes of calculation of the compensation so that the quantum of compensation will decrease with
the increase in the size of the holding. It has also been decided that for the purpose of determining the normal gross
produce of the lands acquired, the value of gross produce as furnished in the return filed by the landowner under the
Tamil Nadu Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1955 (Tamil Nadu Act V of 1955), shall be taken account. It has also been
decided that the compensation payable for any building, machinery, plant, etc., acquired under the Act shall be the
written down value determined in accordance with the provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (Central Act 43 of 1961),
of such building, machinery, plant, etc., on the date of the publication of the notification under section 18(1). The revised
formula for determination of the compensation will take effect on and from the date of the publication of the amending
Act, that is, to lands which vest in the Government after the date of publication of the amending Act.

9. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above objects.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 12th August 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Sixth Amendment Act,
1972 (Tamil Nadu Act 7 of 1974). - Under existing section 18(3) of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on
Land) Act, 1961 (Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
), the surplus land vests in the Government with effect from the date of the publication of the notification under
sub-section (1) of section 18. This notification is published after all the procedural formalities are complied with. Though
section 7 prohibits that no person should hold land in excess of the ceiling area after the date of the commencement of
the Act, by reason of sub-section (3) of section 18, the owner continues to be in possession of the surplus land after the
date of the commencement of the Act and before the date of the vesting of the surplus land in the Government. In some
cases, this period ranges to some years, during which the owner continues to enjoy the surplus land. It has been
suggested that having regard to the spirit of the land reform measure, the surplus land as finally declared by the
competent authority should vest in the Government even from the date of the commencement of the Act which is the
crucial date for the purposes of fixing the ceiling area and that the owner of the land or any person deriving benefit
therefrom should be made liable to pay to the Government an amount as compensation for the use and occupation of
the land for the period for which he was in possession of the surplus land. Clause 3(2) seeks to achieve this object.

2. Under section 22, any transfer made after the date of the commencement of the Act, but before the notified date is
declared as void by the authorised officer if such transfer defeats the provisions of the Act. Under section 10(4), owner
has the option to choose the land which is to be included within his ceiling area. In many cases the owners of land, who
have transferred the land during the period mentioned in section 22, have indicated in their return their desire that the
land so transferred and which transfer has been declared as void, should be taken over by the Government as surplus
land. This results in a double advantage to the land owner, namely, that in addition to the consideration received by him
from the purchaser, he is entitled to compensation from the Government for such surplus land. The Government have
decided that such unintended benefit should not enure to the owner of land and that lands declared as void under
Page 6/83
 
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961
section 22 should be compulsorily included within the ceiling area of the transferor by the authorised officer, without
affecting the rights of the transferee. The result will be that the purchaser will not be disturbed from the possession of his
land and the transferor will not be entitled to any compensation. Clause 3(1) of the Bill seeks to achieve this object.

3. Under section 21-A as amended by clause 3(8) of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Third
Amendment Bill, 1972, partition is permissible between 15-2-1970 and 2-10-1970. The intention is that the partitions
effected to defeat the purpose of the Act made after 2-10-1970 and during the period referred to in section 22 should not
be permitted. Clause 4 of the Bill seeks to achieve this object.

4. A new section 88-A is proposed to be inserted providing for punishment for those persons who have-specified in their
return that the lands, the transfer of which was declared void under section 22, should be taken over by the Government
as surplus land of the transferor. Clause 5 seeks to achieve this object.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 4th December 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Fifth Amendment Act, 1972
(Tamil Nadu Act 10 of 1974). - Under section 73(vii) of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act,
1961, lands converted on or before the 1st day of July 1959 into orchards or topes or areca nut gardens are exempt
from the Ceiling Act so long as they continue to be orchards, topes or areca nut gardens. The High Court has held in
State of Madras v. Thadikkara Vanniar (C. R. P. No. 859/67) that plantain is a fruit bearing tree falling under the
definition of the term "tope" in section 3(47) of the Act and consequently lands grown with plantain crops on the first day
of July 1959 may become eligible for exemption from the ceiling law. The Government have, therefore, decided to
exclude plantain from the definitions of the terms "orchards and tope" so as to bring the lands grown with plantain crops
within the ceiling law.

2. Under section 73(iii) of the Act, any land owned by such cO-operative societies (other than societies registered or
deemed to have been registered under the Tamil Nadu Cooperative Societies Act, 1932 or under the Travancore-Cochin
Co-operative Societies Act, 1951), as are approved by the Government are exempt from the provisions of the ceiling
law. The Government have decided that the above provision should be amended so as to confine the exemption only to
any land assigned by the Government to, and held by, any Land Colonisation Co-operative Society.

3. Under section 73(vi) of Tamil Nadu Act
58 of 1961
, all plantations in existence on the date of the commencement of the Act are exempt from the ceiling law. Similarly,
under section 73 (viii), any land used exclusively for growing fuel trees on the date of the commencement of the Act is
exempt from the ceiling law. The date of the commencement of the Act with reference to the principal Act was 6th April
1960 and consequently plantations and fuel trees that were in existence on 6th April 1960 in any area other than the hill
area were exempt from the ceiling law. Further, under section 31 of the Act, any plantation could be permitted to hold
any land interspersed among or contiguous to such plantation, up to 20 per cent of the extent of such plantation winch
existed on 6th April 1960. By the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Reduction of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1970 (Tamil Nadu Act
17 of 1970), the definition of the date of the commencement of the Act in clause (11) of section 3 of the principal Act was
modified as 15th day of February 1970. Consequently, the exemption in respect of plantations specified in section 73(vi)
and fuel trees specified in section 73(viii) should be construed to apply to the extent of plantations and fuel trees as were
in existence on 15th February 1970. The exemption in respect of lands in hill areas has been withdrawn with effect from
1st March 1972. The Government have now decided that the exemption in respect of plantations and fuel trees should
be restricted to the extent of plantations and fuel trees that were in existence on 6th April 1960 and that the permission
to be granted under section 31 of the Act to any plantation to hold additional extent of land should be restricted to 20 per
cent of the extent of such plantation as was in existence on 6th April 1960.

4. The Bill seeks to give effect to the above objects.
Published in Part IV-Section 1 of the Tamil Nadu Government Gazette Extraordinary,dated the 22nd August 1972.
Statement of Objects and Reasons - Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Amendment Act, 1973
(Tamil Nadu Act 8 of 1974). - Under section 82 of the Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961,
the Land Commissioner may call for and examine the record of any Authorised Officer in respect of any proceeding
under the Act not being a proceeding in respect of which a suit or an appeal to the Land Tribunal is provided, to satisfy
himself as to the regularity of such proceedings or the correctness, legality or propriety of any decision or order passed
thereon, and if in any case it appears to the Land Commissioner that any such proceeding, decision or order should be
modified, reversed or remitted for reconsideration, he can pass orders accordingly.
Page 7/83
 
Tamil Nadu Land Reforms (Fixation of Ceiling on Land) Act, 1961

2. The Act does not prescribe any time-limit within which the parties can invoke the revisionary powers of the Land
